**STEP 1 - Scene:** A bowl of whole raw almonds (a snack, not a full meal), photographed from above at a slight angle.

**STEP 2 - Ruler:** The vessel is a white round plate or bowl, about 18 cm in diameter (roughly side-plate size). Area = 3.14 × 9² ≈ 254 cm².

**STEP 3 - Items:** Whole almonds only. No oil or sauce is visible.

**STEP 4 - Area:** Almonds cover the central part of the plate, about 60% of the vessel area (≈152 cm²).

**STEP 5 - Volume:** The pile is about 1.3 cm high on average (one to two almonds deep). 152 cm² × 1.3 cm ≈ 198 ml.

**STEP 6 - Grams:** Whole almonds have a bulk density of about 0.6 g/ml. 198 ml × 0.6 ≈ 119 g. A count check gives a similar figure: about 80–90 visible almonds at roughly 1.2 g each is about 100 g. I take about 100 g as the best estimate.

**STEP 7 - Energy:** Raw almonds are about 579 kcal/100 g. 100 g × 5.79 ≈ 579 kcal.

**STEP 8 - Sanity check:** About 100 g of almonds, roughly 80–90 nuts, covering most of a small plate, is plausible. Energy of about 580 kcal is consistent with almonds being very energy-dense.
